verification_report.summary: All lemmas, theorems, and intervening deductions pass sequential verification under the five stipulated internal premises. Stretching supplies every required convex competitor and preserves singularity order. Finite-rooftop noncollapse correctly optimizes masses independently over bounded-difference representatives; the subsequent argument establishes class membership. Strict domination correctly obtains the coefficient-one ordered-contact estimate, and its exponential-order and scalar-uniqueness consequences follow. The weighted lower-semicontinuity lemma works for arbitrary smooth backgrounds: constant truncations are Omega-psh, their signed theta products have uniformly capacity-controlled total variation at each fixed level, and the cutoff identifies the positive extended measure before monotone convergence. In the fixed-measure theorem, disjoint first-contact pieces preserve domination without a factor counting obstacles. Positive relative lower mass prevents stretched collapse, and the B=2b construction preserves every prefix index while producing a common relative lower envelope for one extracted sequence. Upward stability proves membership of the L1 limit; weighted lower semicontinuity and strict domination identify the tail-rooftop limit. Squeezing yields capacity convergence, and the common lower envelope supplies uniform raw-tail control for weak measure convergence. The arbitrary-subsequence argument establishes both convergences for the original sequence. The reconstruction attribution matches Sections 3–4 and Theorem 4.2 of [XL26](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.13446v1). No separate global metric positive-volume property or full Li existence theorem is used or inferred.
